title: story-refinery bundle
description: Single source of truth for one refined backlog item. Tracker payloads and agent briefs are projections of this document, never hand-edited independently. NOTE: nothing in this skill runs a JSON Schema validator - scripts/validate.py is the enforcer and checks more than this file can express (dependency cycles, contract ordering, file ownership, coverage). This schema exists for editor completion and for other tools that consume the bundle.

coverage.description: criterion id -> subtask ids. Derived; validate.py recomputes it.

source_text.description: The original ask, verbatim. Scope creep is detected against this.

technical_notes_human.description: What changes, where, what was decided. Every path cited.

follow_ups.description: Work this refinement creates for later: non-goals with a ticket, decisions whose answer changes the next story, and every flag or migration that needs an item to end it. SER002 links these to the tickets the text itself promises.

trigger.description: An observable condition, not a date. Dates in a backlog are wishes.

series.description: Where this story sits in a stream. Predecessors are the bundles its dossier was inherited from - see references/series.md and `evidence.py inherit`.

non_functional.description: Give a number or the word 'unchanged'. Never leave a key blank.

tracker_meta.description: Phase 1. What the tracker already says about this item, copied verbatim before refining: labels, components, type, priority, status, reporter, links. Never invented, and never edited to make a triage rule match. Also what stops a push from deleting the labels somebody set (emit.py carries them through).

triage.description: Phase 1. What those labels change about the refinement. Written by `triage.py apply --write` from the triage.labels policy; enforced by validate.py TRI gates.

route.description: incident: the labels say refinement is the wrong instrument right now (TRI002). Stabilise, then refine what is left.

kind.description: feature | bug, when the labels settle it.

profile.description: Decomposition profile the labels imply, e.g. bugfix for a production finding (TRI005).

require_dimensions.description: Extra intake dimensions these labels demand (TRI004).

mandatory_subtask_kinds.description: Subtask kinds that must exist, e.g. a reproducing test (TRI003).

must_answer_nfr.description: Quality attributes that cannot be blank or 'unchanged' here (TRI006).

add_critics.description: Critics the labels add to the Phase 8 panel, e.g. operator, security (TRI008).

ask.description: Questions these labels raise; written into open_questions with source 'triage'.

unknown_labels.description: Labels no rule and no ignore pattern covers (TRI007) - nobody decided whether they matter.

mitigation.description: What reduces it. A risk without one is a worry (RSK001).

detection.description: The alert, metric or report that tells you it is happening. Required in practice for high severity (RSK002) - otherwise you hear it from a customer.

source.description: Where the risk came from, e.g. premortem, critic finding F3, incident history.

decision_table.description: Phase 3. The only form of criteria that can be proved complete: every combination of condition values is a rule, an impossibility, or a hole validate.py names (DT001).

when.description: condition id -> value, or "*" for any.

then.description: The expected outcome for this combination.

impossible.description: Combinations that cannot occur. Same shape as a rule's 'when'. Use it rather than inventing an outcome for a state the system cannot reach.

impact.description: Phase 1. Goal -> actor -> impact -> deliverable [P: Adzic, Impact Mapping, 2012]. The answer to a ticket that named a mechanism without an outcome, recorded as a chain rather than prose.

goal.description: Measurable, with a number and a date (IMP002). It is what tells you afterwards whether this worked.

impacts.description: The behaviour change in each actor that moves the goal.

deliverables.description: What we build to cause the impact. The least important column, and the one tickets usually start from.

spike.description: Subtask id. Required when status is deferred.

waiting_for.description: deferred: the information that would decide this. An option nobody can tell has matured never gets exercised (DEC008).

expires.description: deferred: the event or date after which deferring costs more than deciding - the last responsible moment [P: Maassen & Matts, Commitment, 2013]. Required (DEC007): an option without an expiry is not a held option, it is an unmade decision.

dimension.description: Intake dimension this question resolves, if any.

intake.description: Was there enough information to refine? Written by intake.py, confirmed by the reader, enforced by validate.py INT gates.

domain.description: Cynefin [P: Snowden & Boone, 2007]. Enough information is not enough knowledge: in a complex domain the honest output is a probe, not a plan (CYN001).

domain_rationale.description: Why that domain. One sentence, arguable.

evidence.description: present: a verbatim quote from source_text

heuristic.description: true until a reader confirms the matched snippet

question_id.description: missing: a blocking question; assumed: a non-blocking one

ruled_out.description: Negative results: what refinement looked for and did not find. The most expensive thing a refinement learns and the first thing compression discards - an implementor who does not know a helper is absent will hunt for it, and may 'find' the wrong one (EVI008/EVI009).

claim.description: What is absent, stated as a fact.

looked_in.description: Paths, globs or queries. A negative result nobody can re-check is a rumour.

conclusion.description: What an implementor should do given the absence.

glossary.description: Domain words as they are used here. An implementor with no context reads them as the industry does, which is often not what this codebase means.

evidence.description: path:line. An uncited convention is a training prior, not a house rule.

repo.description: Only when the contract lives in another repo than the brief's own.

ruled_out.description: Negative results: what refinement looked for and did not find. The most expensive thing a refinement learns and the first thing compression discards - an implementor who does not know a helper is absent will hunt for it, and may 'find' the wrong one (EVI008/EVI009).

claim.description: What is absent, stated as a fact.

looked_in.description: Paths, globs or queries. A negative result nobody can re-check is a rumour.

conclusion.description: What an implementor should do given the absence.

glossary.description: Domain words as they are used here. An implementor with no context reads them as the industry does, which is often not what this codebase means.

preflight.description: Commands that verify the brief's anchors still hold before work starts. Anchors drift between refinement and implementation; an agent that cannot tell its brief is stale implements against it anyway (BRF013). On failure: stop and report, never improvise.

stop_and_ask.description: Conditions under which the implementor must stop rather than decide. 'forbidden' says what not to touch; this says what not to decide (BRF014).

review.description: Phase 8. What hostile, blind readers found in the story and its subtasks, and what was done about each finding. Enforced by validate.py REV001-REV009.

method.description: critics = the blind panel. rubber-duck = the solo fallback: one voice, full context, lower assurance - say so in the handover.

bundle_digest.description: sha256 over the bundle minus 'review' and 'generated_at', written by `review.py digest --stamp`. Proves which content was actually reviewed (REV007).

attempted.description: For a rubber-duck pass that raised nothing: what you tried to break, and why it held.

tailoring.description: Which team-tailoring skill's house rules produced this bundle, what they changed, and what they turned off. See references/tailoring.md; enforced by TLR001-TLR005.

source.description: The tailoring skill's name. Must match tailoring.source in refinery.yaml (TLR001).

mechanism.description: config: a key in refinery.yaml. prompt: judgement applied while reading the tailoring skill. gate: a validator rule.

key.description: Required for mechanism 'config': the key that actually enforces it. If it is unset, the rule only reads as enforced (TLR002).

overrides.description: Anything of this skill's that the team turned off or down. An override naming an invariant is refused (TLR003).

of.description: What is overridden: a config key, a validator code, or an invariant id.

authorised_by.description: A person. 'The team skill says so' is not a person (TLR004).

refused.description: true when the tailoring asked for something an invariant forbids and it was refused.

id.description: implementer | tester | archaeologist | sequencer | stakeholder, or a house critic.

context.description: fresh = a sub-agent that never saw the reasoning. same-session = you re-reading the packet as them, which is weaker and is disclosed.

attempted.description: What this critic tried to break and why it held. The only accepted form of a clean report (REV004).

critic.description: Must be one of the recorded critics (REV009).

severity.description: blocking = an implementer would build the wrong thing, or a stated fact is false.

locator.description: Path into this bundle, e.g. subtasks[3].agent_brief.done_when[0]. It must resolve (REV005).

claim.description: What is wrong, in one sentence.

failure.description: The concrete thing that goes wrong downstream if it ships as is: who does what, and what they get.

resolution.description: What was done. Required for accepted and disputed (REV003).

accepted_by.description: Who accepted the risk. An acceptance only you made is an open question, not an acceptance.
